<reason>A wins by defining the relevant tools as those pooling non-public rival data through a common pricing hub, answering the no-agreement and discretion objections with the hub-and-spoke and cartel-cheating comparisons, and showing scrutiny is a trigger to inspect hidden pooling rather than automatic liability. B's scope and concerted-action challenges were strong, but B did not overcome A's distinction from public-data, accounting, or MLS tools, or A's circularity point that demanding proof before scrutiny would shield outsourced coordination.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>Most decisive was A's Rebuttal 2: the facts B demands before scrutiny sit inside the platform, and holding rent through vacancies is profitable only if the algorithm assures rivals will also hold, turning B's profit and discretion defenses into evidence of coordination.</best_rebuttal>
